{"id":"mimid-1wgh.4.79.12","title":"external_receivers cannot actually be changed, so the hub's HPKE key cannot rotate","description":"Found by code review, 2026-11-26, and verified.

## The contradiction

The `ExternalReceivers` doc in mimi-mls says the list is "changed by
AppDataUpdate, not by a GroupContextExtensions proposal (decision
mimid-1wgh.4.79.4)". Decision mimid-1wgh.4.79.7 leans on the same
assumption: "Rotating the key means an AppDataUpdate per room, which is
work this decision does not do."

Neither is true today:

- `mimi_protocol::components::is_known_component` (components.rs:329)
  covers the policy components, `room_metadata`, `franking_agent` and
  `MLS_BUILT_IN` = [0x0001, 0x0002, 0x0003]. 0x0007 is in none of them.
- So update.rs refuses any AppDataUpdate naming 0x0007.
- GroupContextExtensions proposals are refused outright (decision
  mimid-1wgh.6.2).

`external_receivers` is therefore immutable for a room's lifetime: it
can only be set at creation. With one HPKE pair per hub (decision
mimid-1wgh.4.79.7), a hub that has to replace its pair -- compromise,
or a ciphersuite change -- cannot do it for any existing room. Every
such room would have to be recreated.

## What to decide

Whether 0x0007 becomes a known component, so an AppDataUpdate can change
it. That is not automatic: `apply_commit_op` defines the §4.7
application logic per component, and external_receivers would need its
own -- full replacement is the obvious reading, but who may propose it is
a policy question the room policy does not currently answer. An
external receiver list a member can rewrite is a list a member can point
at itself.

Until that is decided, fix the two places that claim otherwise: the
`ExternalReceivers` doc and decision mimid-1wgh.4.79.7's consequences
section. A doc that describes a capability the code refuses is worse
than one that admits the limitation.

## Not urgent, and why

No room requires the semiprivate format yet, and mimid members cannot
send one (bead mimid-1wgh.4.79.3). The first deployment that uses it is
the point at which rotation has to work, so this is ahead of need -- but
the two misleading claims should go now.","status":"open","priority":2,"issue_type":"bug","owner":"mark@reviewcommit.com","created_at":"2026-11-27T03:02:07.554017883Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","updated_at":"2026-11-27T03:02:07.554017883Z","labels":["feature"],"dependencies":[{"issue_id":"mimid-1wgh.4.79.12","depends_on_id":"mimid-1wgh.4.79","type":"parent-child","created_at":"2026-11-27T03:02:07.610339866Z","created_by":"Mark Atwood","metadata":"{}"}]}

{"design":"## The design, worked out 2026-11-26

Making 0x0007 mutable is safe only together with a check that does not
exist yet, and the order matters.

### What the policy should be

protocol-07 L1582: a SemiPrivateMessage is "encrypted for the members
and the hub provider as the sole external_receiver". So for a MIMI room
the rule is already decided and is the one check_external_receivers
enforces: the list is exactly the hub, and nobody else. There is no
policy question about WHO may proposeedit it, because any proposal that
changes the list to anything but the hub is refused whoever sends it.

That also answers the risk this bead raised. A member adding ITSELF as
an external receiver gains nothing -- a member already reads
handshakes. The risk is a member adding a THIRD PARTY outside the
group, and the exactly-the-hub rule refuses that.

### The gap that makes it unsafe today

check_group, which contains check_external_receivers, is called from
exactly one place: Hub::create_room (hub/mod.rs). It never runs on a
Commit. That is harmless while the component cannot change, and it is
why nothing has noticed.

So the work is, in this order:

1. Run the external_receivers check on every Commit that changes the
   component, not only at room creation. Without this, step 2 lets a
   member rewrite the list unchecked.
2. Add 0x0007 to is_known_component and give it §4.7 application logic.
   Full replacement is the obvious reading: the list is small and has no
   per-entry identity to merge on.
3. Only then can the hub rotate its HPKE key, by proposing an
   AppDataUpdate per room as an external sender.

Doing 2 before 1 would be a regression: it would open a path for a
member to point a room's handshakes at a party of its choosing, which
is exactly what the component being immutable currently prevents.

### Whether to do it at all

Not yet. No room requires the semiprivate format, mimid members cannot
send one, and the hub cannot process one (bead mimid-1wgh.4.79.13). The
first deployment that uses SemiPrivateMessage is when rotation has to
work. Until then the immutability is a limitation to document, which is
done."}
